 17 Nov BLOG: Drury students provide assistance for Election Day
 By Cris Belvin Campus News 0 Drury University > Campus News > BLOG: Drury students provide assistance for Election Day 
 Five Drury students assisted the Greene County Clerk’s Office during the recently completed Nov. 3 General Election.
 Nate Brower (Nixa, Missouri), Caden Harrington (Ozark, Missouri), Bryson Humphries (Owasso, Oklahoma), Jaxson Humphries (Owasso, Oklahoma), and Garrett Salt (Oologah, Oklahoma) each performed a variety of tasks for the County Clerk both on election night and in the days leading up to the big day.
 The students were involved in preparing voting equipment, testing the equipment, and loading updated ballots in the days leading up to the election. On Election Day, students worked as rovers, travelling between different polling locations throughout the county and providing assistance to election workers.
 “Overall, I really enjoyed the experience and appreciated the opportunity to learn more about how elections operate,” Brower said.
 A Cyber Risk Management major with a minor in Computer Science, Brower was fascinated to learn firsthand exactly how elections work.
 “The most interesting part of this opportunity was getting to see how elections operate behind the scenes,” he said. “Before working on the election, I did not fully realize how much preparation and coordination went into making sure everything ran smoothly.”
 Brower thinks everyone should take the opportunity to volunteer in their local elections.
 “Being involved in both the preparation and Election Day operations gave me a greater appreciation for the people who work behind the scenes,” he said. “I believe everyone should have a better understanding of the election process because many people do not realize the extent of the work that goes into keeping elections safe, secure, and organized.”
 Green County Clerk Chief Deputy Amanda Kutter said she was happy to see Drury students taking advantage of an opportunity to get involved.
 “We are so appreciative of their willingness to serve and be part of the election process,” she said. “It’s always wonderful to see young people getting involved in their community, and we are grateful for Drury’s support.”
